_revised: 2026-09-05, same day: the transcription was faithful but the notes were stale. The two color-analysis files contradicted each other, the chino plan prescribed a Western-preppy slim cut that works against the stated goal, and nothing in the folder said what the target register actually is. This file now carries both layers and says which is which: fields marked as facts (size, brands) are still transcription; direction, palette, silhouette, hair and buyNext are a styling judgement made against photographs, and can be argued with.
_excluded: Appearance.md from the same folder is deliberately never transcribed here or anywhere in this repo: it names real people and must never enter a public project.
_gaps: OPEN TEST — undertone. Hold something gold and then something silver, palm-sized or larger, directly under the chin. Daylight at a window, all lamps off, exposure locked. Watch the skin under the jaw, not the metal: gold better = Dark Autumn, silver better = Dark Winter, no clear winner = neutral, in which case `core` is the whole palette. Until then `palette.conditional` stays unresolved. Nothing on `buyNext` depends on the answer as long as charcoal is taken over camel and cream.
The wardrobe direction is written against photographs, not a fitting. Anything about how a specific garment actually falls on him is unverified until something is tried on.

Outfit_Planner.md carried one entry, on Monday: white chunky sweater, 90s light denim, loafers, gold small hoop earrings, trench coat. It is kept here rather than in his planner because the earrings and the chunky-knit-plus-trench combination read as someone else's outfit — possibly Eunice's, possibly saved inspiration. Nothing is lost; it just should not stand as Philipp's Monday until he confirms it.

Trouser model names shift every season. The chino plan holds the brands and the cut; the specific SKUs in the original note are already partly superseded and should be re-checked in store rather than trusted here.

direction.thesis: Hair-led, silhouette-second, logo-never. Most of the effect is settled at the head before a garment is touched; the clothes then hold a vertical, tonal column with a defined shoulder. Nothing here depends on being thin — it depends on line.
direction.builtFrom: Three facts about him, not a look: colouring that is Dark and high-contrast, a 25 cm waist-to-hip drop, and a face that reads a decade younger than the passport. Those decide the palette, the trouser cut, and how far the styling may mature. Everything else follows from them.
direction.onTheOriginalFraming: This was first written in Korean-actor vocabulary, because that is what was asked for. Almost none of it actually depended on that — the palette comes from his colouring, the cut from his measurements, the hair from his face shape. The label was dropped on request; the substance did not change.
direction.ageRead: Reads early-to-mid 30s in photographs, not 43: full hairline, even skin tone, no deep static lines. The clothes are currently the oldest thing in the picture. That widens the range rather than narrowing it — the limiter is context (school, parent evenings, Germany), not the birth year, and over-mature styling would hand back years the face has not lost.

notThis.why: Sheer fabric, embellishment, stage pieces — the idol register the Anson Lo photo pointed at. That is stage costume rather than a wardrobe, and it reads as costume in the room where most of these clothes are actually worn.

direction.referencesNote: These are visual shorthand, not a destination. They are useful because their colouring and build sit close to his, so what works on them transfers directly — not because the goal is to look Korean.

references.name: Gong Yoo
references.why: Closest thing to a template: structured ease, volume in the hair, tonal and quiet.

references.name: Hyun Bin
references.why: Same age bracket, and the coat-over-knit silhouette is near-exactly the target.

references.name: Park Seo-joon
references.why: For the younger read the face actually supports — relaxed tailoring, nothing costume about it.

direction.readOfCurrentPhotos: Four photographs, four sets of functional clothing: sport tee, polo, sport tee, printed sweatshirt. Not a taste problem — a control problem. Nothing in the set is a chosen silhouette. What already works: the gum-sole Sambas, and navy, which appears in three of four and flatters in all three. What works against him: the printed sweatshirt (busy, boxy, adds volume exactly where the training is removing it) and visible athletic branding outside the gym.

hair.priority: The single biggest lever — roughly 60% of the effect is decided before any garment is chosen. Hair either rounds the face or lengthens it, and nothing worn below the collar can undo that.
hair.current: Short, flat on top, growing forward, no taper at the sides and no volume at the crown. It rounds the face and takes height away.
hair.cut: Two-block — 7–10 cm on top, sides tapered rather than shaved. If the name does not land at the barber, ask for length and volume on top with the sides tapered short but not clipped.
hair.shape: Soft side sweep or a loose middle part, with lift at the crown
hair.color: One step softer than the current hard black: dark brown with a warm undertone
hair.product: Matte clay, not gel. Blow-dry lift from underneath first — glossy is a decade out of date.
hair.why: Vertical lift lengthens the face and gives the jaw its line back. Hard black next to skin raises contrast and sharpens every irregularity; shaved sides would read harder than intended and add years the face has not earned.

palette.type: Dark — deep and high-contrast. Undertone open, leaning warm.
palette.confidence: Depth and contrast: established. Undertone: about 60/40 toward warm, which is a leaning and not a diagnosis. Splitting Dark Autumn from Dark Winter needs a controlled gold-versus-silver comparison held at the face, and none of the photographs so far carries one.
palette.established: Near-black hair, dark brown eyes, light-to-medium skin, high hair-to-skin contrast. Deep colours hold across every lighting seen so far — black and navy both sit at the face without draining it. This is the half that decides most of the wardrobe, and it is settled.
palette.open: Warm versus cool. The two candidates are Dark Autumn and Dark Winter. Both are Dark seasons and share most of their palette, which is why this stays open without blocking anything: see `core` for what holds either way.
palette.rule: Low contrast within an outfit, deep tones throughout. Depth is the rule that carries; the undertone only decides the edges.

conditional.note: These depend on the open undertone question. Buy from `core` until it is settled; these are the two ways the edges could go.

avoid.name: Fuchsia
avoid.why: Out for both — too light and too bright against this depth

avoid.name: Lemon yellow
avoid.why: Light and bright — disappears next to near-black hair

avoid.name: Ice pink
avoid.why: Pale and washed — the opposite of a Dark palette

avoid.name: Mid grey
avoid.why: Not wrong, just inert — mid tones flatten a high-contrast face. Go darker.

rules.why: Hip 105 cm over waist 80 cm is a 25 cm drop. A slim cut pulls at the seat and advertises exactly the ratio the training is working on; straight falls clear of the hip and lengthens the leg.
The taper is being built in the gym. Outerwear with a real shoulder seam — overshirt, coat, unstructured blazer — anticipates it instead of waiting for it.
One depth of colour head to foot reads as height. Splitting light-over-dark cuts the body in half at the waist, which is the one place not to draw a line.
A long unbroken vertical is the most reliable lengthening device there is. Double-breasted adds width across the chest and works against it.

rules.rule: No visible branding outside the gym
rules.why: Sport logos say 'on the way to train'. The clothes should not be doing that when the destination is a classroom.

rules.rule: Relaxed, never skinny — and never baggy
rules.why: Easy through the leg, clean at the line. Tight reads dated and fights the hip; oversized reads borrowed and loses the shoulder the whole silhouette is built on.

buyNext.why: Replaces the printed sweatshirt outright. The slight shoulder structure does work a sweatshirt physically cannot, and it goes over anything already in the wardrobe.

buyNext.item: Fine-gauge merino knit, crew or mock neck
buyNext.why: The base layer the whole tonal column is built on. Uniqlo is already on the brand list and their merino is exactly the right weight.

buyNext.colors: Charcoal — safe whichever way the undertone goes. Cream only once it is settled warm.
buyNext.why: The actual silhouette change. This is the piece that does more than the other four combined.

buyNext.colors: Charcoal — safe either way. Camel only once the undertone is settled warm.
buyNext.why: The signature garment of the reference set, and it works unchanged from a school corridor to an evening out.

buyNext.item: One clean leather shoe beside the Sambas
buyNext.why: Derby or chelsea. Shoepassion is already on the list and the size is already known — 8.

seasonalWardrobe.note: Rewritten 2026-09-05 into the target register. The original was generic Autumn-type advice; this is the same four-season structure with the resolved palette and the straight-leg correction applied.
seasonalWardrobe.styleNote: Natural fabrics — wool, cotton, leather. The rule that carries every season: one depth of colour throughout, and a defined shoulder on whatever is outermost.

seasons.heading: Light layers, one tone
seasons.tops: Fine merino or cotton knit in navy or cream, worn under rather than alone
seasons.outerwear: Overshirt or unlined coach jacket in deep olive or charcoal
seasons.bottoms: Straight chinos in cream or stone
seasons.shoes: Sambas, or a dark brown derby when the day needs it

seasons.heading: Cut, not exposure
seasons.tops: Boxy-but-clean linen or linen-blend shirt in cream or slate blue, short sleeve with a proper shoulder seam
seasons.bottoms: Straight trousers in stone, or wide-leg shorts to just above the knee — not sport shorts
seasons.shoes: Clean white leather sneaker or a woven loafer

seasons.heading: The strongest season for this palette
seasons.tops: Merino crew or mock neck in chocolate, forest or burgundy
seasons.outerwear: Overshirt layered under a camel or charcoal coat
seasons.bottoms: Straight trousers in charcoal, or dark denim with no fading

seasons.heading: Long lines, deep tones
seasons.tops: Heavier knit in navy or charcoal, mock or turtleneck
seasons.outerwear: Knee-length single-breasted wool coat, charcoal or camel
seasons.bottoms: Straight wool-blend trousers in charcoal or black

chinoPlan.goal: End goal: capsule wardrobe largely in Ralph Lauren — collector's brand, kept because it means something to him, not because the styling requires it
chinoPlan.midGoal: Interim: a pragmatic mix — Dockers (budget), Suitsupply (midrange), Ralph Lauren (premium)
chinoPlan.fit: Straight leg, mid-to-high rise. Ask for the straight or relaxed cut by fit, not by model name.

revision.change: Fit corrected from Slim Fit + Mid-Rise to Straight + Mid-High-Rise. Brands and the Ralph Lauren end goal stand.
revision.why: The original prescription came from preppy convention and was justified in the note as balancing a longer torso and a small stomach. Against a 25 cm waist-to-hip drop it does the opposite: slim pulls at the seat and shortens the leg line. This is the one correction in the file that rests on a measurement rather than on taste. Only the cut changed.
